title.value: Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies
title.justification: The title 'Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies' was chosen as it is the precise title provided under which the paper is published.
title.quote: Title of the paper 'Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies'.

extractions.description: The paper discusses a novel evaluation methodology for offline reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms, named Sequential Evaluation (SeqEval). It aims to provide insights into data efficiency and robustness to dataset distribution shifts by evaluating algorithms as a function of training set size. Unlike traditional evaluation that focuses on compute steps, SeqEval evaluates based on data, providing a more applicable means of comparison with online RL algorithms. The approach offers practical applications in any domain dependent on offline RL for policy optimization, including robotics and potentially climate or sustainability-related systems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: Sustainable Development, specifically climate or ecological impact, is not a central theme of this paper. The central theme revolves around improving evaluation methodologies in reinforcement learning, which could potentially be applied to various domains including climate systems, but is not directly addressed.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: A crucial challenge for current deep RL algorithms is that they require a tremendous amount of environment interactions for learning. This can be infeasible in situations where such interactions are expensive, such as in robotics.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not focus directly on sustainable development themes but on evaluation methodologies for RL. Any applicability to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development is indirect and not explicitly covered within the paper's scope.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we propose a sequential approach to evaluate offline RL algorithms as a function of the training set size and thus by their data efficiency.

secondary_categories.justification: As the primary category was 'N/A', there are no notable secondary categories that align with climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: Offline RL algorithms try to address this issue by bootstrapping the learning process from existing logged data without needing to interact with the environment from the very beginning.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the paper's focus is not centered on Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development, there is no appropriate sub-category to classify it under the hierarchical list provided.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our approach is generally applicable and easy to implement. We compare several existing offline RL algorithms using this approach and present insights from a variety of tasks and offline datasets.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As the primary sub-category was 'N/A', there are no notable secondary sub-categories that align with climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Sequential evaluation provides valuable insights into the data efficiency of the learning process and the robustness of algorithms to distribution changes in the dataset while also harmonizing the visualization of the offline and online learning phases.

applications.justification: There are no specific applications mentioned in the paper related to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: We call this approach of evaluation Sequential Evaluation (SeqEval) and present settings where SeqEval can be integrated into the evaluation protocol of offline RL algorithms.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need to create a new category as the subject matter of this paper does not directly contribute to Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development categories.
new_primary_category.quote: In this paper, we propose a sequential style of evaluation for offline RL methods so that algorithms are evaluated as a function of data rather than compute or gradient steps.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-category options provided were sufficient, but none applied to the content of this paper, hence no new sub-category suggestion is necessary.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This approach allows us to study the sample efficiency and robustness of offline RL algorithms to distribution shifts.
